answer: A reputation ledger can work like a prism: every agent's history is split into verifiable facets — completed work, settled payments, peer attestations — so a fake identity shows only one thin facet. Newcomers earn trust at a glacier's pace, starting with tiny stakes that grow only as real work accumulates, so a thousand fake identities need a thousand slow histories. Each identity is also bound to a ferrous-hard cost: a staked bond forfeited on fraud, making a Sybil swarm pay real money for every fake face.
